name: Horn of Arra'chea
summary: The Horn of Arra'chea is a hunting trophy taken from the legendary kodo Arra'chea, who wanders the plains of Mulgore. Claimed at the behest of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the horn serves as definitive proof that an aspiring hunter has the discipline and tracking prowess to provide for the Shu'halo.

sections.title: A Chieftain's Test
sections.body: Though passing the initial Rites of the Earthmother grants a youth their rightful place atop Thunder Bluff, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof expects his people to continually prove their worth. For the tauren, identity is bound directly to the hunt and their enduring harmony with the land. Cairne tests young hunters by tasking them with tracking down Arra'chea, a massive, lone kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking Arra'chea's horn proves mastery over the fundamental art of tracking prey across vast distances.

sections.title: Providing for the Tribe
sections.body: Bringing the horn to the high rise of Thunder Bluff is more than a display of martial strength; it serves the survival of the entire community. In tauren culture, nothing of a slain beast is allowed to go to waste. Presenting the trophy alerts the High Chieftain to the fallen beast's location, allowing gathering parties to quickly depart down into the plains to harvest Arra'chea's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

faq.q: What is the Horn of Arra'chea?
faq.answer: It is a horn taken from Arra'chea, a powerful and elusive kodo that roams the plains of Mulgore. Hunters bring it to Cairne Bloodhoof as a rite of passage to demonstrate their tracking skills.

Arra'chea is a renowned kodo bull that circles the grasslands northeast of Thunder Bluff. Known for his strength and wide migratory route, he serves as a formidable quarry for hunters looking to prove their worth to the tribe.

faq.q: Why does Cairne Bloodhoof ask for this trophy?
faq.answer: Cairne believes that maintaining one's standing in Thunder Bluff requires continuous proof of service and capability. By tracking and felling Arra'chea, a hunter proves their dedication to the traditions of the Earthmother and provides valuable resources for the community.

faq.q: What happens to the rest of the beast after it is killed?
faq.answer: In accordance with tauren custom, no part of the hunted animal is squandered. Once the horn is delivered to confirm the kill, Cairne dispatches a gathering party down into Mulgore to collect the hide and meat for Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: Presenting this horn to High Chieftain Cairne marks a crucial rite of passage, confirming your readiness to sustain and defend your people atop Thunder Bluff.
Tracking Arra'chea's circular path across the broad expanse of Mulgore tests fundamental stalking and wilderness survival skills prized by any true hunter.
